label: tests-run-at-head-before-approve
name: No evidence that a test exercising the changed path ran at this head, in every build configuration it touches
description: What breaks: the approval rests on reading alone. Multi-command changes under #ifdef FWD_HW_RESULTS with no statement that the other build was tried (2915270383 'Did you sanity test that?'); timeout and sentinel changes with a test plan listing only clang-format (4265644124 'Approved, but please run at least a subset of representative UTs'); a shared_ptr shard pushed onto two edges, so Wade asks whether multi-user runs were done (3156090573); his own practice of running the suite on the branch and pasting the ctest summary before approving (4131374395: 69 tests; 4422833076: 13 binaries). Procedure: for every changed region inside #ifdef X with an #else or #ifndef twin, require a body sentence that the opposite build was run; when the body's test plan is static only and the diff touches production constants or hardware-facing code, ask for a representative UT run; when a bot raises a high-severity path finding, ask for the run that exercises that path; with machine access, run the labelled binaries and paste the summary.
disposition_reason: Check 3 asks whether an assertion executes on the gating lane; this widens the theme to whether any run happened at all, including the opposite build configuration and hardware-labelled tests CI cannot run.
agent_feasibility: partial: the static part (ifdef twin untested, static-only test plan) is mechanical; the run itself needs a machine with the hardware labels.

members.concern: Before merging, the author should run at least a representative subset of the unit tests (UTs) against the change; Wade conditions his approval on that.

detection.trigger: The PR body's test plan lists only static checks (clang-format, whitespace) and leaves 'CI green' unchecked, while the diff changes production constants or hardware-facing code paths (here h/pos/config.hpp timeouts, h/pos/hwattention.hpp sentinel).
detection.procedure: Read the PR body test-plan checklist and `gh pr checks N`; list the test targets under t/ that exercise the touched headers (grep t/ for the touched symbols or include paths); check whether the body or a comment reports any of them run on this head.
detection.question: Does any statement on the PR (body, comment, CI status) show that a unit test exercising the changed code ran and passed at this head?

members.quote: Approved, but please run at least a subset of representative UTs against these changes before merging.
members.note: Posted as a COMMENTED review, not an APPROVED state, so the 'Approved' word is prose only. Wade had himself run 13 test binaries one minute earlier (issue-comment 4422833076) and posted the PASS list. Final APPROVED state came on 2026-05-21 at head 159e09a940 after mcherba answered the inline question.

members.concern: Approval with two justifications: (a) a regression judgement - the known intermittent multi-user crash is not caused by this branch's content, so there is no regression relative to the base feature branch; (b) he ran the whole unit-test suite (69 ctest tests, labels fake/fpga/hugepages/main) on the branch himself and pasted the ctest summary including the five disabled tests.

detection.trigger: A PR that touches hardware/FPGA or scheduler paths whose body says WIP or names an open crash/hang, and whose CI lane cannot execute the hardware-labelled tests.
detection.procedure: Build the branch head on a machine with the hardware (here the fpga label needs FPGA cards) and run `ctest` for all labels; paste the '100% tests passed, N tests failed out of M' summary, the per-label time table and the 'did not run (Disabled)' list verbatim. Separately, read the body's stated open problem (multi-user hang) and decide whether its cause is inside the diff; cite the external finding used for that judgement.
detection.question: Do all unit tests, including the hardware-labelled ones CI cannot run, pass at the head, and is the open crash attributable to this diff or to something outside it?

members.concern: Wade endorses the Cursor bot's finding that a shard spanning the split point is pushed onto both the intermediate and the child edge via shared_ptr and so is visited twice during traversal, and asks the author whether multi-user tests were run to see the duplicate-shard assertion.

detection.trigger: A hunk inserts the same shared object into two containers that one traversal visits in sequence (here `intermediate->parent_edge.shards.push_back(s); child->parent_edge.shards.push_back(std::move(s));`), or a bot/agent review raises a high-severity double-visit finding on such a hunk.
detection.procedure: Find the traversal that walks both containers (grep `shard_stack`, `shards_getting_gofs`, `compute_forward_args` in h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp) and the duplicate guard it asserts ('duplicate shard in shards_getting_gofs'). If the shared object reaches the guard from both containers, the finding stands. Then ask for the runtime scenario that exercises it (multi-user, repeated iterations) by name, since the PR body's repro is single-user (`--users 1 --iterations 10`).
detection.question: Can the same shard object reach the duplicate assertion from both edges in one traversal, and has a run that exercises that path (multi-user, repeated iterations) been done?

members.concern: The multi-command changes sit under #ifdef FWD_HW_RESULTS (the build mode where hardware attention results are forwarded directly); Wade asks whether the change also works in the build with that macro undefined and whether the author sanity-tested that path.

detection.trigger: The diff changes code inside an #ifdef X region of a file that also has #ifndef X or #else regions on the same feature, and the PR body or commit messages describe testing in only one configuration.
detection.procedure: grep the touched file for '#ifdef X', '#ifndef X', '#else' pairs on the same macro; list which regions the diff changed. Read the PR body's test command and the commit subjects for which configuration was built. If the sibling region shares state the diff changed (buffers, indices, counts), ask whether the other configuration was built and run.
detection.question: Does the build with this macro in the opposite state still compile and produce correct results after this change, and was it run?

members.quote: do these changes for multi-command work when `FWD_HW_RESULTS` is UNdefined as well? Did you sanity test that?
members.note: At 8f22c93862 self_attention.hpp defines FWD_HW_RESULTS at line 19 and has paired #ifdef/#ifndef regions at lines 331-1108 (e.g. #ifndef at 908, 961, 1070). The PR body shows one runtron command, no mention of the other configuration. No reply in the digest. Check 3 is about hardware-gated test assertions on CI; the shared theme is 'a path the stated testing does not execute', but the trigger (a runtime early exit in a TEST_CASE) does not fire here. Identifying the question is agent-reviewable; answering it needs a build and a run.

codex_bullets.bullet: Check whether the lock protects the actual shared state at its mutation boundary. A caller-side lock may miss another caller or serialize an independent wait. Ask for evidence before changing lock placement.
codex_bullets.reason: Four comments (PRs 2777, 2233, 2565). 3277240111 gives the full reasoning (co-locate the lock, finer grain, independent waiters, future drift) and ends by deferring to the owner. No Claude check.

codex_bullets.bullet: Exercise the production entry point when the change is orchestration. Direct helper calls do not establish grouping, reservation handoff, completion, or drain behavior.
codex_bullets.reason: Three comments (PRs 4128, 2903, 2565). No Claude check asks whether the test goes through the production dispatch path.

codex_bullets.bullet: Trace compilation, test selection, assertion reachability, and recorded execution separately. Move hardware-independent checks outside unnecessary hardware gates where practical. Apply the current repository's CI policy.
codex_bullets.reason: Four Wade comments (PRs 4557, 2698, 2011, 1920) plus the 3879 paste. Claude check 3 already states the four facts.
